paper_title: Cool-3D: An End-to-End Thermal-Aware Framework for Early-Phase Design Space Exploration of Microfluidic-Cooled 3DICs

scenario.figure_or_table: Table VI and Fig. 9 (baseline chip, Splash2 fft, steady-state HotSpot 7.0 heat maps)
scenario.description: Baseline 3-layer 3DIC (bottom core layer with 4 cores and shared L2, two 4x4 memory-bank layers above) with a passive heat sink and no microfluidic cooling, evaluated with the gem5 + McPAT + CACTI-3DD + HotSpot 7.0 Cool-3D flow. Heat maps per layer are shown for the fft benchmark, with maximum temperatures of 395.52 K, 392.83 K and 390.57 K for the core, middle memory and top memory layers.
scenario.architecture: 4 out-of-order 8-issue cores at 2 GHz; L1 I/D caches 4KB/8KB 2-way; shared 2MB L2; 8GB memory with 32 banks (8 banks per rank); 3 layers: bottom cores 0-3 (2x2), middle memory banks 0-15 (4x4), top memory banks 16-31 (4x4)
scenario.workload: Splash2 fft benchmark (default problem size) from the Splash2 suite
scenario.operating_point: Passive heat sink, no microfluidic cooling; steady-state thermal simulation; 2 GHz core clock; per-block power values and floorplan dimensions are not given numerically in the paper

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 7.0 steady-state thermal simulation (pdf p.9-10), fed by gem5 performance, McPAT core/cache power and CACTI-3DD memory power
original_setup.optimizer: None; no automatic optimizer. Design changes are made manually in case studies (stacking order, microfluidic cooling pattern, L2 size). RL-based optimization is listed as future work (pdf p.13)
original_setup.controller: None; no dynamic thermal management or runtime controller is described. Steady-state analysis only
original_setup.benchmark: Baseline 3-layer 3DIC (bottom: 4 cores + shared L2; middle and top: 4x4 memory-bank layers), 4 O3 8-issue cores at 2 GHz, passive heat sink, no microfluidic cooling, running Splash2 fft at default problem size (Table VI pdf p.9; Fig. 9 pdf p.10)

thermal_observable.location: Bottom core layer (cores 0-3) of the baseline stack, Splash2 fft, from the Fig. 9 heat map (pdf p.10); the middle memory layer maximum is 392.83 K and the top memory layer maximum is 390.57 K
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum temperature over the layer's heat map in the steady-state HotSpot 7.0 simulation, as labelled in the figure. The paper uses the maximum over the whole 3D stack as its comparison metric in Case Study I (pdf p.10)

physical_mismatches.reason: Paper provides no numeric floorplan geometry (x, y, width, height) for any block; Fig. 9 shows only a labelled heat-map layout with no dimensions, and die area is not stated. A Studio floorplan cannot be built without inventing coordinates.
Paper provides no per-block power values for the fft baseline; McPAT and CACTI-3DD outputs are not tabulated, and total chip power is not given. Splitting power would require an unpublished rule.

The scenario is a 3-layer 3D stack with a core layer under two memory layers. A 2D or single-die Studio model cannot represent the vertical stacking, layer-to-layer coupling, or the 3D layer-ordering effects the paper studies.

Cooling in the baseline is a passive heat sink whose HotSpot 7.0 package parameters are not published. Case studies II-III add microfluidic cooling layers (vertical and 90-degree bent channels), which a Studio model may not support.

The original flow chains gem5, McPAT, CACTI-3DD, and HotSpot 7.0, with per-block power derived from workload simulation. Studio cannot reproduce that upstream power generation, so the thermal solve is only an approximation of the HotSpot 7.0 step.
The paper has no transient, controller, optimizer, or reliability component in the selected baseline scenario, so there is no mismatch from those; only a steady-state solve is relevant.

studio_assumptions: No complete experiment can be extracted: the floorplan is returned empty because no block geometry or power rows are published in the paper packet.
Any Studio package, material, heat-sink, and ambient-temperature assumptions would be bundled defaults and not from the paper; none are asserted for the Cool-3D baseline.
No exact replication of the paper's HotSpot 7.0 result is claimed.
missing_inputs: Numeric floorplan geometry (x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m) for core-layer blocks (e.g., C0_IC, C0_FPU, L2_shared) and memory banks B_0-B_31; not given in the paper, only a labelled heat-map layout in Fig. 9
Per-block power (W) for the Splash2 fft baseline scenario; neither McPAT nor CACTI-3DD outputs are tabulated
HotSpot 7.0 configuration: heat-sink, spreader, TIM, material properties, ambient temperature, grid resolution

Cool-3D GitHub repository (https://github.com/iCAS-SJTU/Cool-3D, pdf p.1 and p.13): the paper says release is 'in process'; no asset was bundled in the packet (assets list empty), so existence of its inputs is unverified
Splash2 benchmark repository (https://github.com/liuyix/splash2benchmark, pdf p.14): no asset bundled in the packet; and it holds benchmark source, not thermal inputs
gem5, McPAT, CACTI-3DD configuration files and the unified front-end input for the baseline
